questions.question: For how many positive integers n ≤ 1000 is n² + n + 1 divisible by 7?
questions.solution: Check residues mod 7: n ≡ 0,1,2,3,4,5,6 give n² + n + 1 ≡ 1, 3, 0, 6, 0, 3, 1. So 7 divides it exactly when n ≡ 2 or 4 (mod 7). 1000 = 7 × 142 + 6, so each residue class appears 142 times in 1..994, and 995..1000 have residues 1..6, which include 2 and 4 once each. Total = 2 × 142 + 2 = 286.

questions.question: When 125! is written in base 12, how many zeros does it end with?
questions.solution: 12 = 2² × 3, so the number of trailing zeros is the largest k with 12ᵏ dividing 125!, i.e. min(⌊v₂/2⌋, v₃). v₂(125!) = 62 + 31 + 15 + 7 + 3 + 1 = 119, so ⌊119/2⌋ = 59. v₃(125!) = 41 + 13 + 4 + 1 = 59. Both limits give 59, so 125! ends in 59 zeros in base 12.

questions.question: What is the remainder when 2²⁰²⁶ + 3²⁰²⁶ is divided by 13?
How many ordered pairs of integers (x, y) satisfy x² − y² = 2026?
questions.solution: x² − y² = (x − y)(x + y). The two factors x − y and x + y differ by 2y, so they are both even or both odd. Both odd gives an odd product; both even gives a multiple of 4. But 2026 = 2 × 1013 is even and not a multiple of 4, so no integer pair works: 0.

questions.question: For how many integer values of k does the equation x² + kx + 24 = 0 have both roots integers?
questions.solution: If the roots are integers p and q, then pq = 24 and k = −(p + q). The factor pairs of 24 are (1, 24), (2, 12), (3, 8), (4, 6) and the same pairs with both signs negative, giving p + q = ±25, ±14, ±11, ±10. These are 8 different values of k.

questions.question: A function f satisfies f(x) + 2f(2 − x) = 3x for every real x. What is f(5)?
questions.solution: Replace x by 2 − x: f(2 − x) + 2f(x) = 3(2 − x) = 6 − 3x. Call f(x) = a and f(2 − x) = b: a + 2b = 3x and 2a + b = 6 − 3x. Doubling the second and subtracting the first: 3a = 12 − 9x, so f(x) = 4 − 3x and f(5) = −11. (Check: f(5) + 2f(−3) = −11 + 26 = 15 = 3 × 5 ✓.)

questions.question: How many integers x with |x| ≤ 20 satisfy (x − 2)(x − 5)(x − 9) < 0?
questions.solution: The cubic changes sign at 2, 5 and 9; it is negative for x < 2 and for 5 < x < 9. Integers from −20 to 1: 22 of them. Integers 6, 7, 8: 3 more. Total 25 (x = 2, 5, 9 give 0, which is not < 0).

questions.question: If log_a b = 2 and log_b c = 3 (a, b, c > 1), what is log_c (abc)?
questions.solution: Write everything as powers of a: b = a², c = b³ = a⁶. Then abc = a¹⁺²⁺⁶ = a⁹ and c = a⁶, so log_c(abc) = 9/6 = 3/2.

questions.question: What is the sum of all three-digit numbers that leave remainder 3 when divided by 7?
How many five-digit numbers have digits that add up to 10?
questions.solution: Let the digits be d₁…d₅ with d₁ ≥ 1. Put e = d₁ − 1, so e + d₂ + … + d₅ = 9 with every term ≥ 0: C(13, 4) = 715 solutions. A digit cannot exceed 9; the only way to break that here is e = 9 (d₁ = 10) with the rest 0, which is 1 solution. So 715 − 1 = 714.

questions.question: In how many ways can 10 identical chocolates be given to 4 children so that every child gets at least 1 and no child gets more than 4?
questions.solution: Give each child 1 first; now share 6 more with each child getting 0 to 3 extra. Without the upper limit: C(9, 3) = 84. Subtract cases where some child gets 4 or more extra: fix that child at ≥ 4, leaving 2 to share among 4: C(5, 3) = 10, times 4 children = 40. Two children cannot both get 4 (that needs 8 > 6). So 84 − 40 = 44.

questions.question: Two fair dice are thrown. What is the probability that the product of the two numbers is a perfect square?
questions.solution: Perfect-square products from 1–36 with both factors from 1 to 6: equal numbers (1,1) … (6,6) give 6 outcomes, and 1 × 4 = 4 gives (1,4) and (4,1). No other pair works (e.g. 2 × 8 is impossible, 9 = 3 × 3 already counted). 8 favourable outcomes out of 36 = 2/9.

questions.question: A triangle has sides 13 cm, 14 cm and 15 cm. What is the radius (in cm) of its circumcircle? (Enter as a decimal.)
questions.solution: s = 21, so by Heron's formula the area is √(21 × 8 × 7 × 6) = √7056 = 84. Circumradius R = abc/(4 × area) = 2730/336 = 65/8 = 8.125.

questions.question: How many points with integer coordinates lie strictly inside the circle x² + y² = 25?

Two trains start at the same moment from towns A and B, 300 km apart, towards each other, and meet after 2 hours. The faster train reaches the other town 1 hour 20 minutes after the meeting. How many minutes after the meeting does the slower train reach its destination?
questions.solution: Before meeting, together they cover 300 km in 2 h, so u + v = 150. After meeting the faster train covers the slower train's 2-hour stretch, 2v, in 4/3 h: 2v/u = 4/3, so u = 1.5v. Then 2.5v = 150 gives v = 60, u = 90. The slower train must cover the faster train's stretch 2u = 180 km at 60 km/h: 3 hours = 180 minutes. (Shortcut: T² = t₁t₂, so t₂ = 4/(4/3) = 3 h.)

questions.question: A and B together can finish a job in 10 days, B and C in 12 days, and C and A in 15 days. All three start together, but A leaves after 4 days and B and C finish the job. How many days does the job take in all?
questions.solution: Adding the three rates: 2(A + B + C) = 1/10 + 1/12 + 1/15 = (6 + 5 + 4)/60 = 1/4, so A + B + C = 1/8 per day. In 4 days they do 4/8 = 1/2 of the job. B + C do 1/12 per day, so the other half takes 6 days. Total 4 + 6 = 10 days.

questions.question: A container holds 80 litres of pure milk. Some litres are taken out and replaced with water; this is done three times in all, the same quantity each time. The container finally has 33.75 litres of milk. How many litres were taken out each time?
questions.solution: After three replacements, milk = 80(1 − x/80)³ = 33.75, so (1 − x/80)³ = 33.75/80 = 0.421875 = (3/4)³. Hence 1 − x/80 = 3/4 and x = 20.

questions.question: A sum lent at compound interest (compounded yearly) amounts to ₹7,260 after 2 years and ₹7,986 after 3 years. What is the sum (in ₹)?
questions.solution: The third year's interest is 7986 − 7260 = 726 on 7260, so the rate is 10%. Then P × 1.1² = 7260 gives P = 7260/1.21 = 6000.

questions.question: In a survey of 100 people, 70 like tea, 75 like coffee and 80 like juice. What is the smallest possible number of people who like all three?
questions.solution: Count dislikes: 30 do not like tea, 25 not coffee, 20 not juice. Someone who misses all three must dislike at least one, so at most 30 + 25 + 20 = 75 people miss at least one drink. So at least 100 − 75 = 25 like all three, and 25 is reached when the three groups of dislikers do not overlap.

questions.question: How many odd divisors does 10! have?
questions.solution: 10! = 2⁸ × 3⁴ × 5² × 7. An odd divisor uses no factor 2, so it is 3ᵃ5ᵇ7ᶜ with a ≤ 4, b ≤ 2, c ≤ 1: 5 × 3 × 2 = 30.

questions.question: What is the remainder when 1! + 2! + 3! + … + 100! is divided by 24?
questions.solution: From 4! = 24 onwards every factorial is a multiple of 24, so only 1! + 2! + 3! = 9 matters. The remainder is 9.

questions.question: A right-angled triangle has hypotenuse 15 cm and inradius 3 cm. What is its area in cm²?
questions.solution: For a right triangle, r = (a + b − c)/2, so a + b = 15 + 6 = 21. Also a² + b² = 225. Then 2ab = 21² − 225 = 216, so ab = 108 and the area is ab/2 = 54. (The legs are 9 and 12.)

questions.question: How many points (x, y) with integer coordinates satisfy |x| + |y| ≤ 5?
questions.solution: For each x from −5 to 5, |y| ≤ 5 − |x| gives 2(5 − |x|) + 1 values of y: x = 0 gives 11, x = ±1 give 9, ±2 give 7, ±3 give 5, ±4 give 3, ±5 give 1. Total = 11 + 2(9 + 7 + 5 + 3 + 1) = 61.

questions.question: Three of the six vertices of a regular hexagon are chosen at random. What is the probability that they form an equilateral triangle?
questions.solution: There are C(6, 3) = 20 ways to choose three vertices. An equilateral triangle needs every other vertex: {1, 3, 5} or {2, 4, 6} — only 2 choices. Probability = 2/20 = 1/10.
